description: IgnisAI is a solo AI project focused on making NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to explore and understand. I am an MS AI researcher with experience in LLMs, RAG, multimodal AI and model evaluation. The goal is to build an interactive dashboard that retrieves, ranks and summarizes findings while grounding AI-generated insights in supporting evidence for reliable fire safety research.
summary:
IgnisAI is a web dashboard that helps engineers and researchers use NASA's microgravity fire experiments to make crewed spacecraft and future Moon and Mars bases safer. It organises all 24 combustion investigations in NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database, including BASS, Saffire, SAME, FLEX and ACME, into one clear table of fuels, test conditions, hardware and measurements. Every value links to the NASA sentence it came from.

Users can filter and compare investigations and rank them for a chosen environment (spacecraft, space station, lunar or Martian base, or pressurized rover) using open, visible rules. They can also ask questions answered by AI only from NASA records, with a citation for every claim. When the records don't cover something, such as partial gravity, the app says so.

This matters because Moon bases are expected to use 30 % oxygen, which makes materials more flammable. IgnisAI shows that almost no tested conditions match that atmosphere, pointing to the experiments still needed.
details:
What it does
IgnisAI is a web dashboard that turns NASA's microgravity combustion experiments into fire-safety evidence for crewed spacecraft, space stations, and future Moon and Mars bases. It brings together all 24 investigations in the Combustion Science area of NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database. It has four views:

  • Investigations: one table with objectives, fuel, fuel phase, shape and size, oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow speed, diluents, gravity, hardware, measurements, test variables, fire-safety pillar (prevention, detection, suppression), and the kind of fire-safety equipment each investigation informs. You can filter it and download it as CSV for modelling.
  • Compare: two or three investigations side by side.
  • Relevance ranking: choose a spacecraft, space station, lunar base, Martian base or pressurized rover, and the investigations are ranked by five visible rules: fire-safety objective, fuel realism, atmosphere overlap, cabin airflow and gravity relevance. An evidence-gap chart plots tested oxygen against pressure next to the expected Moon-base atmosphere (30 % oxygen at 10.2 psi).
  • Ask the records: a question is matched to PSI passages, and an AI model answers only from those passages, citing a record for every claim.

How it works
A Python script downloads the PSI records through PSI's public data service and extracts fields with fixed text rules. Every value links to the sentence it came from. When a record does not state a value, the app shows "Not reported in source" and never guesses.

Benefits and impact
Engineers and researchers can find which experiments matter for a given habitat in minutes instead of reading dozens of reports. The evidence-gap chart shows that only 2 of 24 investigations report both oxygen and pressure, and none tested the Moon-base atmosphere. That points directly to the experiments NASA still needs, such as LUCI and FM2.

What makes it creative
Rankings depend on the environment, the scoring rules are fully visible, and the app treats missing data honestly. It shows where the evidence ends instead of covering the gaps with AI-generated text. For partial gravity, which PSI has no data on, it says so clearly.

Factors considered

  • Scientific integrity: sources are always visible, missing values stay missing, and AI answers are kept separate from source text.
  • Usability for students and engineers.
  • Accessibility: dark theme with readable contrast.

Tools
Python, Streamlit, pandas and Altair; the open-weight model gpt-oss-120b via Groq; GitHub and Streamlit Community Cloud.

Code: https://github.com/AzkaQadir/IgnisAI
dataRefs: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI): Combustion Science investigations
PSI: Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS)
PSI: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME)
